verdict.rationale: CoreWeave offers CKS, a managed Kubernetes service on bare metal. Clusters can be created via the Cloud Console, Terraform, or the API, and support node pools, autoscaling and kubectl access. SUNK runs Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes, so batch training goes through Slurm while services run on Kubernetes, removing the need to build a custom scheduler. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CKS/SUNK scheduling; deeper SUNK documentation (e.g., how managed it is, how it is set up, and how Slurm partitions or queues are configured).
